newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, break four-session rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, break four-session rally.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index ended lower on Thursday, depressed by a weak bond market, ending a four-session rally on Canada's biggest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 17.32 points to close at 5558.86 in heavy turnover of 96.02 million shares worth C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion).
Solid corporate earnings and the prospect of a Canadian interest rate cut had pushed the TSE to daily records since last Friday.
But the streak ended with today's downturn in North American bonds, said Jim Doak, director and senior vice-president of investment research for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
"The U.S. bond market reversed around midday and I think a lot of people took their lead from that," Doak said.
Canadian bonds underperformed their U.S. counterparts as investors took profits amid disappointment that the Bank of Canada did not cut interest rates today.
Gold, consumer product and technology stocks led nine of Toronto's 14 sub-groups lower. Conglomerates and base metals led the strong side.
The overall market finished mixed with advancing stocks edging out declines 471 to 456 with 300 issues unchanged.
* Newbridge Networks Corp. led weak high-tech issues, falling 3.20 to 41.80 on 2.3 million shares. The stock was hit by investor concerns over Newbridge's upcoming second quarter results.

* BCE Inc., Canada's biggest publicly-traded company, sank 0.75 to 61 on 1.9 million shares after soaring on good earnings on Wednesday. BCE also announced plans today to buy back up to five million of its common shares.
* Canadian Pacific Ltd. led conglomerates higher, climbing 0.55 to close at 33.85 after hitting a 52-week high of 34.60.
The railway operator posted strong earnings on Wednesday.
* CGC Inc. led net gainers, closing up 3.55 at 10.90.
